theme: The $6.3B Binance hack hits bitcoin and crypto stocks, Intel's guidance drags chips and the Nasdaq into a sharp AI selloff, SpaceX closes below its IPO price as its credit risk hits a record, and Tesla's Texas robotaxi fleet closes in on Waymo.

items.title: Who holds the 20.1M bitcoin: exchanges, ETFs, public companies, governments
items.picked: Hackers stole about $6.3B from Binance on Thursday, including 18,270 bitcoin worth roughly $1.4B, per CoinDesk. Binance says about $3B has been frozen, withdrawals are still suspended, and it plans to publish updated proof-of-reserves on Monday, Nov 2.
items.matters: The hack puts custody back in focus, and this chart shows how much bitcoin sits with exchanges compared with ETFs, companies and governments.
items.know: The tab's latest row (Oct 14 2026) has 2.676M BTC on exchanges, 1.297M in US spot ETFs, 1.304M at public companies, 0.599M with governments, an estimated 1.1M for Satoshi and 13.122M with everyone else, out of 20.098M in circulating supply. The 18,270 BTC stolen is roughly 0.7% of the exchange total. The data predates the hack, government holdings are filled for the latest row only, and the Satoshi figure is an estimate.

items.title: Strategy's market cap vs the value of its bitcoin (mNAV)
items.picked: Strategy, Coinbase and Robinhood fell between 7.2% and 10.6% on Friday after the Binance hack, per Reuters, a day after Strategy reported its Q3 results.
items.matters: When mNAV is below 1, the stock is worth less than the bitcoin Strategy holds, which makes it harder to sell new shares to buy more bitcoin without diluting holders.
items.know: On Oct 16 the tab has mNAV at 0.894x, a $61.82B diluted market cap against $69.11B of bitcoin. It was 1.009x on Oct 2, hit a low of 0.629x on Jun 26 2026, and was 2.383x in Jan 2025. The data ends Oct 16, so it misses this week's results and Friday's drop, and this mNAV leaves out debt and preferred stock, so it won't match Strategy's own figure.

items.title: Coinbase stock vs bitcoin: relative price and 52-week beta
items.picked: Coinbase was among the crypto stocks that fell 7.2% to 10.6% on Friday after the Binance hack, per Reuters. A hack at the biggest rival can hurt the whole sector even if it pushes some users toward Coinbase.
items.matters: The ratio shows whether owning COIN has beaten owning bitcoin, and the beta shows how much the stock amplifies bitcoin's moves.
items.know: On Oct 16 the tab has COIN divided by BTC at 38.27 (Apr 2021 = 100), its lowest reading since May 9 2025 (34.85); the all-time low in the tab is 33.007 in Apr 2023. COIN's 52-week beta to bitcoin is 1.156. The data is weekly and ends Oct 16, before the hack.

items.title: Chip stocks vs the S&P 500 (SOXX vs SPY, total return)
items.picked: The chip index fell 7.2% on Friday and had a monthly loss of more than 15% after Intel's weak guidance sent its shares down 28.6%, per Reuters. Nvidia fell 4.2% and AMD 10.9%.
items.matters: Chips led the AI rally, so their lead over the S&P 500 is a quick read on how much of the AI trade is unwinding.
items.know: The tab's Oct 2026 point has the chips-to-S&P ratio at 246.48 (Jul 2001 = 100), down from a record 327.76 in Jun 2026, and SOXX 22.95% below its peak on a total-return basis. The data is monthly and the tab doesn't say which day the Oct point is from, so it may not include Friday's drop.

items.title: Quarterly data center revenue: Nvidia vs Broadcom vs AMD vs Intel
items.picked: Intel guided Q4 EPS to $0.25 against a $0.44 estimate and revenue of no more than $16B against $17.1B, per Motley Fool, and Broadcom's 5-year CDS hit a record 175.4bp on Thursday, per ICE data reported by Bloomberg.
items.matters: This shows who is actually collecting the AI data center spending, which matters as investors start asking whether that spending pays off.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the tab has Nvidia data center revenue at $89.02B, Broadcom semiconductor solutions $20.84B, AMD data center $6.72B and Intel data center and AI $6.26B, against $41.1B, $9.17B, $3.24B and $3.94B a year earlier. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, the companies' fiscal quarters don't line up exactly, and Broadcom's segment includes non-AI chips.

items.title: Nasdaq: dot-com run from the Netscape IPO vs AI run from ChatGPT's launch
items.picked: The Nasdaq fell 2.86% on Friday to 25,437, its biggest one-day drop since June 5, and is 7.8% below its Oct 6 record close, per Reuters.
items.matters: Selloffs bring back the 'is this 1999?' question, and this chart lines the two runs up day by day.
items.know: At the tab's latest point, trading day 970 since ChatGPT's launch, the AI-era line is at 232.76 against 238.61 for the dot-com run at the same point. The dot-com run went on to peak at 482.32 on day 1155 before collapsing. The tab doesn't date its last point, so check whether it includes this week's drop, and the two eras had very different rates and earnings.

items.title: Neocloud debt vs cash ($B)
items.picked: Reuters says Friday's selloff was driven by fears about AI cash burn, and the cost of protecting AI-linked debt against default hit records this week, per ICE data reported by Bloomberg.
items.matters: Neoclouds fund their GPUs largely with debt, so when credit tightens, the ones with debt far above their cash are the most exposed.
items.know: The tab has CoreWeave at $35.6B of debt against $5.5B of cash, Nebius $8.5B vs $8B, IREN $7.6B vs $5.9B, Applied Digital $6.3B vs $3B, Cipher $5.4B vs $0.8B and TeraWulf $3.1B vs $2.6B. Most figures are as of Jun 30 2026 (Applied Digital Aug 31, TeraWulf Mar 31). Debt is long-term debt as tagged in filings, Nebius's excludes any current portion, and CoreWeave's large lease liabilities aren't included.

items.title: SPCX price-to-sales since the June 2026 IPO
items.picked: SPCX fell 6.37% on Friday to $134.72, closing below its $135 IPO price, and Yahoo Finance says SpaceX has lost more than $500B of market value since its Oct 6 high.
items.matters: Price-to-sales is the simplest way to see how much future growth is priced into SpaceX, and how much that has come down.
items.know: On Oct 20 the tab has SPCX at 84.55x trailing sales, with a $147.79 close, a $1,948.14B market cap and $23.04B of trailing 4-quarter revenue. The multiple peaked at 144.37x on Jun 16. The data ends Oct 20 and the revenue column hasn't been updated for the Q3 results, which would lower the multiple, and the image is the Oct 19 export.

items.title: SpaceX free cash flow: operating cash flow minus capex
items.picked: The cost of protecting SpaceX debt against default rose about 20bp to a record 266.5bp on Thursday, per ICE data reported by Bloomberg, as credit markets worry about AI spending. SPCX then closed below its IPO price on Friday.
items.matters: SpaceX's capex now far exceeds the cash its businesses generate, so it depends on IPO proceeds and borrowing to keep building.
items.know: For the four quarters to Sep 30 2026 the tab has operating cash flow of $15.762B, capex of $54.96B and free cash flow of -$39.198B, compared with -$13.952B in 2025, -$5.387B in 2024 and +$0.105B in 2023. The Drive export still showed the older TTM to Jun 2026, so this image was redrawn from the sheet.

items.title: Texas robotaxi registrations: Tesla vs Waymo
items.picked: A post trending on X says Tesla now has 1,204 registered robotaxis in Texas (631 Model Y and 573 Cybercabs), 55 behind Waymo's 1,259, while a Forbes piece questions whether Tesla's rides are truly unsupervised.
items.matters: The Texas registry is the only public, vehicle-level count of these fleets, so it's the scoreboard both sides point to.
items.know: The tab, as of Oct 28, has Tesla at 1,080 (507 Model Y and 573 Cybercabs), Waymo 1,207, Avride 344 and Zoox 63. It hasn't been updated to the newer 1,204 vs 1,259 counts. These are registered vehicles, not vehicles carrying riders, and the registry doesn't assign them to cities. The image was redrawn from the tab on Oct 29.
